$comment: Known-bad dependency versions (scripts/audit-lock.mjs, `npm run audit:lock`, also run by `npm run hygiene`). Built from the GitHub advisory matches in PR #491. It works offline: it reads the lockfiles and manifests, not the registry. Each entry names a file (an npm package-lock.json, a Cargo.lock, or a package.json for a dependency range that is not locked), a package, the versions that count as bad (`range`, e.g. "<3.3.16 || >=4.0.0 <5.1.16", or an exact `versions` list) and the advisories. status "fixed": the bad versions are gone; one coming back fails the check. status "open": the bad version is still there and needs an owner step (`fix`, a command that needs the registry or crates.io). It needs an `expires` date (YYYY-MM-DD) at most 90 days from today, after which it fails, and it fails as stale once the bad version is gone (then set it to "fixed"). For a package.json entry, the lowest version the declared range allows is checked.

entries.name: zip
entries.fix: cd src-tauri && cargo update -p tauri-plugin-updater --precise 2.14.1 && cargo tree -i zip && cargo build
entries.note: tauri-plugin-updater 2.14.0 requires zip 4; 2.14.1 moved to zip 9. `cargo update -p zip --precise 9.x` alone fails because 4.6.1 to 9 is a semver-major jump. Cargo.lock needs crates.io checksums, so it cannot be edited offline.
